```{r}
#| label: load-data

# ── Helper: load all CSV/JSON exports from one run directory ────────────────
load_run_data <- function(dir_path, label) {
  dir_path <- normalizePath(dir_path, mustWork = TRUE)

  meta     <- jsonlite::read_json(file.path(dir_path, "metadata.json"))
  df_obj   <- read.csv(file.path(dir_path, "objectives.csv"))

  norm_path <- file.path(dir_path, "objectives_normalized.csv")
  df_norm   <- if (file.exists(norm_path)) read.csv(norm_path) else NULL

  hv_path  <- file.path(dir_path, "hypervolume_evolution.csv")
  df_hv    <- if (file.exists(hv_path)) read.csv(hv_path) else NULL

  pop_path <- file.path(dir_path, "population_stats.csv")
  df_pop   <- if (file.exists(pop_path)) read.csv(pop_path) else NULL

  psel_path  <- file.path(dir_path, "pixel_selection.csv")
  df_psel    <- if (file.exists(psel_path)) read.csv(psel_path) else NULL

  elig_path  <- file.path(dir_path, "eligible_pixels.csv")
  df_elig    <- if (file.exists(elig_path)) read.csv(elig_path) else NULL

  obj_names     <- unlist(meta$objective_names)
  raster_shape  <- unlist(meta$raster_info$shape)   # c(nrows, ncols)

  # Objective normalisation scales (for annotation, not applied here)
  norm_scales <- tryCatch(
    unlist(meta$algorithm$objective_normalization$scales),
    error = function(e) NULL
  )

  # Invert minimised objectives whose values are negative for easier interpretation.
  # Objectives containing "anomaly" or "connectivity_gain" were minimised and are
  # stored as negative; negate them so that larger = better throughout all downstream plots.
  invert_cols <- grep("anomaly|connectivity_gain", obj_names, value = TRUE)
  if (length(invert_cols) > 0) {
    df_obj[, invert_cols] <- -df_obj[, invert_cols]
    if (!is.null(df_norm)) df_norm[, intersect(invert_cols, names(df_norm))] <-
      -df_norm[, intersect(invert_cols, names(df_norm))]
  }

  list(
    label        = label,
    dir          = dir_path,
    meta         = meta,
    obj_names    = obj_names,
    n_obj        = length(obj_names),
    n_solutions  = meta$n_solutions,
    n_nondom     = meta$n_nondominated_solutions,
    raster_shape = raster_shape,
    norm_scales  = norm_scales,
    df_obj       = df_obj,
    df_norm      = df_norm,
    df_hv        = df_hv,
    df_pop       = df_pop,
    df_psel      = df_psel,
    df_elig      = df_elig
  )
}

run_a <- load_run_data(RUN_DIR_A, LABEL_A)
run_b <- load_run_data(RUN_DIR_B, LABEL_B)
run_c <- load_run_data(RUN_DIR_C, LABEL_C)
run_main <- run_a  # primary run displayed in Part 1 (single-run sections)

# Use run_a's objective names as canonical; warn if they differ

if (!identical(obj_names, run_b$obj_names)) {

obj_labels <- gsub("_", " ", obj_names) %>% tools::toTitleCase()
```

# Initial state

```{r}

files <- c(
  Abiotic_Anomaly = "../inputs/abiotic_condition_anomaly.tif",
  Biotic_Anomaly = "../inputs/biotic_condition_anomaly.tif",
  #Landscape_Anomaly = "../inputs/landscape_condition_anomaly.tif",
  Implementation_Cost = "../inputs/implementation_cost.tif"
)

rasters <- lapply(files[file.exists(files)], rast)
if (length(rasters) == 0) stop("No raster files found.")
if (length(rasters) < length(files)) message("Some raster files are missing.")

lulc <- rast("W:/EU_BioES_SELINA/WP3/4. Spatially_Explicit_EC/Data/LULC/LULC_2018_agg.tif") |>
  crop(rasters[[1]])
names(lulc) <- "layer"

r <- c(rasters, list(layer = lulc)) %>% rast()

allowed_layers <- c(12, 13, 16, 17) 

df <- as.data.frame(r, xy = TRUE) %>%
  drop_na() %>%
  filter(layer %in% allowed_layers) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(Abiotic_Anomaly, Biotic_Anomaly, Implementation_Cost),
    names_to = "Objective",
    values_to = "Value"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Objective = recode(
      Objective,
      Abiotic_Anomaly = "Abiotic anomaly",
      Biotic_Anomaly = "Biotic anomaly",
      Implementation_Cost = "Implementation cost"
    )
  )

ggplot(df, aes(x = x, y = y, fill = Value)) +
  geom_raster() +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(name = "Value") +
  facet_wrap(~Objective, ncol = 3) +
  coord_equal() +
  theme_sp

```

## Do trade-offs exist in space?

Pairwise spatial similarity (Jaccard index) between non-dominated solutions, plotted against Euclidean distance in normalised objective space.

Negative relationship = solutions with lower spatial overlap correspond to greater differences in objective performance, indicating that trade-offs in the Pareto set are driven by distinct spatial configurations.

::: panel-tabset

## Pareto front

```{r}

#| fig-height: 5
#| fig-width: 14

```

Burden sharing constrains the optimisation, reducing flexibility and eliminating high performing solutions, while forcing a much higher correlation between objectives.
:::

## Spatial priority classification

Each eligible pixel is classified into one of five priority classes based on (a) its mean selection frequency (RFOP) across all runs, and (b) which sensitivity dimension drives the most variation in that frequency.



```{r}
#| label: classification-config

# ── Master run directory list (all condition scenario × seed combinations) ────
# Keys are used as run labels throughout; _seed### is stripped to derive the
# scenario group_label for sensitivity comparisons.
SCENARIO_DIRS <- c(
  global_all_seed100        = "../r_inputs/global_all_seed100",
  global_all_seed101        = "../r_inputs/global_all_seed101",
  global_all_seed102        = "../r_inputs/global_all_seed102",
  global_drop_smd_seed100   = "../r_inputs/global_drop_smd_seed100",
  global_drop_smd_seed101   = "../r_inputs/global_drop_smd_seed101",
  global_drop_smd_seed102   = "../r_inputs/global_drop_smd_seed102",
  global_drop_sbd_seed100   = "../r_inputs/global_drop_sbd_seed100",
  global_drop_sbd_seed101   = "../r_inputs/global_drop_sbd_seed101",
  global_drop_sbd_seed102   = "../r_inputs/global_drop_sbd_seed102",
  global_drop_soc_seed100   = "../r_inputs/global_drop_soc_seed100",
  global_drop_soc_seed101   = "../r_inputs/global_drop_soc_seed101",
  global_drop_soc_seed102   = "../r_inputs/global_drop_soc_seed102",
  global_drop_uzl_seed100   = "../r_inputs/global_drop_uzl_seed100",
  global_drop_uzl_seed101   = "../r_inputs/global_drop_uzl_seed101",
  global_drop_uzl_seed102   = "../r_inputs/global_drop_uzl_seed102",
  global_drop_tsd_seed100   = "../r_inputs/global_drop_tsd_seed100",
  global_drop_tsd_seed101   = "../r_inputs/global_drop_tsd_seed101",
  global_drop_tsd_seed102   = "../r_inputs/global_drop_tsd_seed102",
  global_drop_can_seed100   = "../r_inputs/global_drop_can_seed100",
  global_drop_can_seed101   = "../r_inputs/global_drop_can_seed101",
  global_drop_can_seed102   = "../r_inputs/global_drop_can_seed102",
  global_drop_cdi_seed100   = "../r_inputs/global_drop_cdi_seed100",
  global_drop_cdi_seed101   = "../r_inputs/global_drop_cdi_seed101",
  global_drop_cdi_seed102   = "../r_inputs/global_drop_cdi_seed102",
  global_drop_swf_h_seed100 = "../r_inputs/global_drop_swf_h_seed100",
  global_drop_swf_h_seed101 = "../r_inputs/global_drop_swf_h_seed101",
  global_drop_swf_h_seed102 = "../r_inputs/global_drop_swf_h_seed102",
  global_drop_swf_t_seed100 = "../r_inputs/global_drop_swf_t_seed100",
  global_drop_swf_t_seed101 = "../r_inputs/global_drop_swf_t_seed101",
  global_drop_swf_t_seed102 = "../r_inputs/global_drop_swf_t_seed102",
  global_drop_lai_seed100   = "../r_inputs/global_drop_lai_seed100",
  global_drop_lai_seed101   = "../r_inputs/global_drop_lai_seed101",
  global_drop_lai_seed102   = "../r_inputs/global_drop_lai_seed102",
  global_drop_ndvi_seed100  = "../r_inputs/global_drop_ndvi_seed100",
  global_drop_ndvi_seed101  = "../r_inputs/global_drop_ndvi_seed101",
  global_drop_ndvi_seed102  = "../r_inputs/global_drop_ndvi_seed102",
  upper_q75_all_seed100     = "../r_inputs/upper_q75_all_seed100",
  upper_q75_all_seed101     = "../r_inputs/upper_q75_all_seed101",
  upper_q75_all_seed102     = "../r_inputs/upper_q75_all_seed102"
)

# Derive dimension-specific lists from SCENARIO_DIRS:
#   - indicator: drop-one indicator runs + global_all baseline (same spatial scope)
#   - policy:    global_all (baseline group) + upper_q75_all (policy variant group).
#                Both groups must be present so sens_policy = range(group means) > 0.
#                Without the baseline group, only one group exists → range = 0 → no
#                policy-sensitive pixels ever classified.
#   - seed:      global_all × 3 seeds (isolates stochastic noise); keys renamed to
#                seed100/101/102 so each seed is its own group (stripping _seed###
#                would collapse all three into one group, making nsens_seed = 0)
INDICATOR_RUNS <- as.list(SCENARIO_DIRS[!grepl("^upper_q75", names(SCENARIO_DIRS))])
POLICY_RUNS    <- as.list(c(
  SCENARIO_DIRS[grepl("^global_all_seed", names(SCENARIO_DIRS))],  # baseline group
  SCENARIO_DIRS[grepl("^upper_q75",       names(SCENARIO_DIRS))]   # policy variant group
))
seed_idx       <- grepl("^global_all_seed", names(SCENARIO_DIRS))
SEED_RUNS      <- as.list(SCENARIO_DIRS[seed_idx])
names(SEED_RUNS) <- sub("global_all_", "", names(SEED_RUNS))   # seed100, seed101, seed102
PARAM_RUNS     <- NULL

# Classification thresholds (tune these after inspecting the diagnostic plots)
THRESH_LOW    <- 20    # % — below this → Low priority
THRESH_HIGH   <- 60   # % — above this (+ low sensitivity) → Robust priority
THRESH_STABLE <- 0.3  # normalised sensitivity below which a dimension is negligible

# Which eligible pixel reference to use for grey underlay (must have df_elig loaded)
ELIG_REFERENCE <- run_a
```

```{r}
#| label: classification-load
#| results: hide

# Helper: load all runs in a named list and bind into a single data frame.
# group_label is derived by stripping trailing _seed### from the key so that
# all seeds of the same scenario are averaged into one group before computing
# cross-scenario sensitivity range.
.load_dim_runs <- function(run_dirs, dim_type) {
  if (is.null(run_dirs) || length(run_dirs) == 0) return(NULL)
  dfs <- lapply(names(run_dirs), function(nm) {
    dir <- run_dirs[[nm]]
    if (!dir.exists(dir)) {
      message(sprintf("Directory not found, skipping: %s", dir))
      return(NULL)
    }
    grp <- sub("_seed\\d+$", "", nm)   # e.g. "global_all_seed100" → "global_all"
    load_run_rfop(dir_path = dir, label = nm, dim_type = dim_type, group_label = grp)
  })
  dplyr::bind_rows(Filter(Negate(is.null), dfs))
}

runs_all_df <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  .load_dim_runs(INDICATOR_RUNS, "indicator"),
  .load_dim_runs(POLICY_RUNS,    "policy"),
  .load_dim_runs(SEED_RUNS,      "seed"),
  .load_dim_runs(PARAM_RUNS,     "param")
)

cat(sprintf(
  "Loaded %d pixel-run records from %d unique runs across dimensions: %s\n",
  nrow(runs_all_df),
  length(unique(runs_all_df$run_label)),
  paste(sort(unique(runs_all_df$dim_type)), collapse = ", ")
))
```

```{r}
#| label: classification-compute

if (nrow(runs_all_df) == 0) {
  message("No run data loaded — configure INDICATOR_RUNS / POLICY_RUNS / SEED_RUNS above.")
  class_df <- NULL
} else {
  class_df <- compute_spatial_classification(
    runs_df       = runs_all_df,
    elig_df       = ELIG_REFERENCE$df_elig,
    thresh_low    = THRESH_LOW,
    thresh_high   = THRESH_HIGH,
    thresh_stable = THRESH_STABLE
  )

  class_pct <-  class_df %>%
      dplyr::count(classification) %>%
      dplyr::mutate(pct = round(n / sum(n) * 100, 1))

  #identify what values of classification are available
  available_classes <- unique(class_pct$classification)
  print(available_classes)

  pct_low <- class_pct %>%
  dplyr::filter(classification == "Low priority") %>%
  dplyr::pull(pct)

  pct_robust <- class_pct %>%
  dplyr::filter(classification == "Robust priority") %>%
  dplyr::pull(pct)

  pct_cond <- class_pct %>%
  dplyr::filter(classification == "Condition sensitive") %>%
  dplyr::pull(pct)

  pct_policy <- class_pct %>%
  dplyr::filter(classification == "Policy sensitive") %>%
  dplyr::pull(pct)

  pct_unstable <- class_pct %>%
  dplyr::filter(classification == "Unstable / noisy") %>%
  dplyr::pull(pct)
}
```

| Classification | Definition | Number of pixels |
|----|----|----|
| **Low priority** | Mean RFOP \< `r THRESH_LOW` across all runs: consistently avoided by the algorithm regardless of assumptions. | `r pct_low` |
| **Robust priority** | Mean RFOP ≥ `r THRESH_HIGH` and low sensitivity across all dimensions: selected under most assumptions. | `r pct_robust` |
| **Condition sensitive** | Selection frequency varies most with indicator/condition assumptions (which ecological indicators are included). | `r pct_cond` |
| **Policy sensitive** | Selection frequency varies most with policy decisions | `r pct_policy` |
| **Unstable / noisy** | Selection frequency varies most with random seed: stochastic algorithm noise dominates. | `r pct_unstable` |

Sensitivity for dimension $d$ is normalised as $s_d = \text{range}(\bar{f}_{d,g}) \,/\, (\bar{f}_{\text{all}} + 1)$ where $\bar{f}_{d,g}$ is the mean RFOP per group $g$ within dimension $d$ and $\bar{f}_{\text{all}}$ is the mean RFOP across all runs. The $+1$ prevents division by zero for low-frequency pixels.

```{r}
#| label: classification-diagnostics
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-width: 12

# Diagnostic: distributions of mean RFOP and sensitivity scores.
# Use these to calibrate THRESH_LOW, THRESH_HIGH, and THRESH_STABLE.
if (!is.null(class_df) && nrow(class_df) > 0) {
  p1 <- ggplot(class_df, aes(x = mean_rfop_all)) +
    geom_histogram(binwidth = 5, fill = "steelblue", colour = "white") +
    geom_vline(xintercept = c(THRESH_LOW, THRESH_HIGH),
               linetype = "dashed", colour = c("orange", "darkgreen")) +
    scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 100)) +
    labs(title = "Distribution of mean RFOP across all runs",
         x = "Mean RFOP (%)", y = "Pixel count")

  p2 <- class_df %>%
    tidyr::pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("nsens_"),
                        names_to = "dimension", values_to = "nsens") %>%
    dplyr::mutate(dimension = sub("nsens_", "", dimension)) %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = nsens, fill = dimension)) +
    geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.05, colour = "white", position = "identity", alpha = 0.6) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = THRESH_STABLE, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey30") +
    scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set1", name = "Dimension") +
    labs(title = "Distribution of normalised sensitivity",
         subtitle = sprintf("Dashed line: thresh_stable = %g", THRESH_STABLE),
         x = "Normalised sensitivity", y = "Pixel count")

  p1 + p2 + patchwork::plot_layout(ncol = 2)
}
```

## Pareto front sensitivity

How much does the *quality* of the Pareto front — and the best achievable value on each objective — change across sensitivity dimensions?

Two complementary summaries:

1.  **Hypervolume (HV)** — a scalar indicator of overall Pareto front quality (larger = better). A drop in HV relative to the reference run indicates that removing an indicator or changing a policy assumption restricts the algorithm's ability to find high-quality solutions.
2.  **Ideal-point shift** — the best value the algorithm achieves on each individual objective across the non-dominated front. A shift away from the reference reveals *which specific objectives* are most affected by each assumption.

```{r}
#| label: pareto-sensitivity-config

# SCENARIO_DIRS is defined in the classification-config chunk above.
# Build PARETO_SENSITIVITY_RUNS by loading each run object from those same dirs.
PARETO_SENSITIVITY_RUNS <- lapply(names(SCENARIO_DIRS), function(nm) {
  dir <- SCENARIO_DIRS[[nm]]
  grp <- sub("_seed\\d+$", "", nm)
  # global_all seeds also appear as the seed dimension
  dim <- dplyr::case_when(
    grp == "global_all"  ~ "seed",
    grepl("^upper_q75",  nm) ~ "policy",
    TRUE                 ~ "indicator"
  )
  run <- tryCatch(load_run_data(dir, nm), error = function(e) {
    message(sprintf("  Skipping %s: %s", nm, conditionMessage(e))); NULL
  })
  if (is.null(run)) return(NULL)
  list(run = run, dim_type = dim, group_label = grp)
})
names(PARETO_SENSITIVITY_RUNS) <- names(SCENARIO_DIRS)
PARETO_SENSITIVITY_RUNS <- Filter(Negate(is.null), PARETO_SENSITIVITY_RUNS)

# Reference run: global_all_seed100 (the full-indicator baseline)
PARETO_REF_LABEL <- "global_all_seed100"

if (length(PARETO_SENSITIVITY_RUNS) == 0) {
  message("No runs configured — populate PARETO_SENSITIVITY_RUNS above.")
  pareto_stats_df <- NULL
} else {
  pareto_stats_df <- collect_pareto_stats(PARETO_SENSITIVITY_RUNS, obj_names)
}
```

### Ideal & nadir shift

For each run and objective, the **filled circle** marks the ideal-point % change (best achievable value) and the **open circle** marks the nadir % change (worst non-dominated value), both relative to the reference run. The connecting segment shows how the *width* of the Pareto front changes: a long segment means the front is stretching or compressing, while the segment's position on the x-axis shows whether the whole front shifts. Blue = improved, red = degraded.

# Four-objective run (abiotic × biotic × cost × connectivity)

Connectivity gain is currently included as a precomputed per-pixel metric based on the amount of existing semi-natural habitat within a 100 m neighbourhood of each conversion-eligible pixel.

Restoration is here divided into two action types:

-   **restoration** (improving ecological condition in-situ)
-   **conversion** (changing agricultural land use to semi-natural habitat, directly contributing to connectivity gain).

## Connectivity objective function

For each candidate conversion pixel $j$, the precomputed gain is:

$$
g_j = \sum_{i \,:\, d(i,j) \le R} \mathbf{1}\!\left[\text{LULC}_i \in \mathcal{S}\right]
$$

where $R = 100\,\text{m}$, $\mathcal{S}$ is the set of semi-natural LULC classes, and $d(i,j)$ is Euclidean distance between pixels $i$ and $j$.

Given a binary decision vector $\mathbf{x}_c$ over conversion-eligible pixels, the objective maximised by the algorithm is:

$$
f_{\text{conn}}(\mathbf{x}_c) = \sum_j x_{c,j} \cdot g_j
$$

Pixels embedded in existing semi-natural habitat receive higher $g_j$ and are therefore prioritised over isolated pixels surrounded by agriculture.

```{r}
#| label: config-4obj

# ── Point this at the export_to_r.py output directory for the 4-objective run ──

obj_labels_4 <- gsub("_", " ", obj_names_4) |> tools::toTitleCase()
```

# Effect of seeding on optimisation outcomes

Comparing the effect of seeding with 3 extreme solutions.

```{r}
#| label: comparison stats
cat(sprintf("Run A: %s  (%d solutions, %d non-dominated)\n",
            LABEL_A, run_a$n_solutions, run_a$n_nondom))
cat(sprintf("Run B: %s  (%d solutions, %d non-dominated)\n",
            LABEL_B, run_b$n_solutions, run_b$n_nondom))
```

#### a) Convergence: does seeding accelerate convergence?

Without seeding, the algorithm converges earlier and shows faster improvement over early generations. With seeding, it reaches a higher hypervolume.

```{r}
#| label: compare-hv
#| fig-height: 4

compare_hv_plot <- function(run_a, run_b) {
  if (is.null(run_a$df_hv) && is.null(run_b$df_hv)) {
    cat("hypervolume_evolution.csv not available for either run.\n")
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }
  hv_df <- bind_rows(
    if (!is.null(run_a$df_hv)) mutate(run_a$df_hv, run = run_a$label) else NULL,
    if (!is.null(run_b$df_hv)) mutate(run_b$df_hv, run = run_b$label) else NULL
  ) %>% mutate(run = factor(run, levels = c(run_a$label, run_b$label)))

  run_cols <- setNames(c("#E05C2A", "steelblue"), c(run_a$label, run_b$label))

  hv_a  <- if (!is.null(run_a$df_hv)) tail(run_a$df_hv$hypervolume, 1) else NA_real_
  hv_b  <- if (!is.null(run_b$df_hv)) tail(run_b$df_hv$hypervolume, 1) else NA_real_
  ratio <- if (!is.na(hv_a) && hv_a != 0) hv_b / hv_a else NA_real_

  sub_txt <- sprintf(
    "Final HV: %s = %.4g | %s = %.4g | ratio B/A = %.3f",
    run_a$label, hv_a, run_b$label, hv_b,
    if (!is.na(ratio)) ratio else NaN
  )

  ggplot(hv_df, aes(x = generation, y = hypervolume, colour = run)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
    geom_point(size = 1.2, alpha = 0.6) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = run_cols, name = "Run") +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::scientific) +
    labs(
      subtitle = sub_txt,
      x = "Generation", y = "Hypervolume"
    )
}

compare_hv_plot(run_a, run_b)
```

#### b) Pareto quality: does seeding improve the Pareto front?

Non-dominated solutions from both runs plotted together.

```{r}
#| label: compare-pareto
#| fig-height: 4

compare_pareto_overlay <- function(run_a, run_b, obj_names, obj_labels) {
  k <- length(obj_names)
  if (k < 2) { cat("Need >= 2 objectives.\n"); return(invisible(NULL)) }

  nd_a <- run_a$df_obj[run_a$df_obj$is_nondominated == 1, ] %>% mutate(run = run_a$label)
  nd_b <- run_b$df_obj[run_b$df_obj$is_nondominated == 1, ] %>% mutate(run = run_b$label)
  df   <- bind_rows(nd_a, nd_b) %>%
    mutate(run = factor(run, levels = c(run_a$label, run_b$label)))

  run_cols <- setNames(c("#E05C2A", "steelblue"), c(run_a$label, run_b$label))
  pairs    <- combn(k, 2, simplify = FALSE)

  plots <- lapply(pairs, function(p) {
    xi <- obj_names[p[1]]; yi <- obj_names[p[2]]
    xl <- obj_labels[p[1]]; yl <- obj_labels[p[2]]
    ggplot(df, aes(x = .data[[xi]], y = .data[[yi]], colour = run)) +
      geom_point(size = 2.5, alpha = 0.7) +
      scale_colour_manual(values = run_cols, name = "Run") +
      labs(x = xl, y = yl)
  })

  wrap_plots(plots, ncol = length(plots), guides = "collect") +
    plot_annotation(
      title    = sprintf("Pareto Front Overlay \u2014 %s", toupper(ECOSYSTEM)),
      subtitle = sprintf("%d ND (%s)  +  %d ND (%s)",
                         run_a$n_nondom, run_a$label,
                         run_b$n_nondom, run_b$label),
      theme = theme(plot.title    = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold"),
                    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 11, colour = "grey40"))
    )
}

compare_pareto_overlay(run_a, run_b, obj_names, obj_labels)
```

The C-metric table below quantifies mutual domination. Seeded run outperformed the not-seeded run in terms of dominance.

```{r}
#| label: coverage-table

# C(B, A): proportion of run_a's ND front dominated by at least one solution in run_b
coverage_stats <- function(run_a, run_b, obj_names) {
  nd_a <- as.matrix(run_a$df_obj[run_a$df_obj$is_nondominated == 1, obj_names])
  nd_b <- as.matrix(run_b$df_obj[run_b$df_obj$is_nondominated == 1, obj_names])

  dom_by_b <- mean(apply(nd_a, 1, function(a)
    any(apply(nd_b, 1, function(b) all(b <= a) && any(b < a)))))
  dom_by_a <- mean(apply(nd_b, 1, function(b)
    any(apply(nd_a, 1, function(a) all(a <= b) && any(a < b)))))

  hv_a <- if (!is.null(run_a$df_hv)) tail(run_a$df_hv$hypervolume, 1) else NA_real_
  hv_b <- if (!is.null(run_b$df_hv)) tail(run_b$df_hv$hypervolume, 1) else NA_real_

  # Generational Distance (GD): mean distance from each run's ND front to the
  # combined reference front (union of both ND sets, re-filtered for dominance).
  # GD(A) < GD(B) means run A's front is closer to the combined best-known front.
  combined <- rbind(nd_a, nd_b)
  # Keep only non-dominated rows of the combined set
  is_nd_combined <- !apply(combined, 1, function(p)
    any(apply(combined, 1, function(q) all(q <= p) && any(q < p))))
  ref <- combined[is_nd_combined, , drop = FALSE]

  gd <- function(approx, reference) {
    mean(apply(approx, 1, function(p)
      sqrt(min(colSums((t(reference) - p)^2)))))
  }

  gd_a <- gd(nd_a, ref)
  gd_b <- gd(nd_b, ref)

  tibble::tibble(
    Metric = c(
      sprintf("C(B\u2192A): %% of %s solutions dominated by %s", run_a$label, run_b$label),
      sprintf("C(A\u2192B): %% of %s solutions dominated by %s", run_b$label, run_a$label),
      sprintf("GD (%s): mean dist to combined reference front", run_a$label),
      sprintf("GD (%s): mean dist to combined reference front", run_b$label)
    ),
    Value = c(
      sprintf("%.1f%%", dom_by_b * 100),
      sprintf("%.1f%%", dom_by_a * 100),
      sprintf("%.4g", gd_a),
      sprintf("%.4g", gd_b)
    )
  )
}

knitr::kable(coverage_stats(run_a, run_b, obj_names),
             caption = "C-metric and Generational Distance comparison between runs")
```

#### c) Bias: does seeding shift which part of objective space is explored?

All solutions from both runs for each pair of objectives (colour = run). A systematic positional shift or difference in cloud shape indicates seeding biases the search towards a different region of objective space.

```{r}
#| label: compare-pairwise
#| fig-height: 5

compare_pairwise_scatter <- function(run_a, run_b, obj_names, obj_labels) {
  k <- length(obj_names)
  if (k < 2) { cat("Need at least 2 objectives.\n"); return(invisible(NULL)) }

  df <- bind_rows(
    run_a$df_obj %>% select(all_of(obj_names)) %>% mutate(run = run_a$label),
    run_b$df_obj %>% select(all_of(obj_names)) %>% mutate(run = run_b$label)
  ) %>% mutate(run = factor(run, levels = c(run_a$label, run_b$label)))

  run_cols <- setNames(c("#E05C2A", "steelblue"), c(run_a$label, run_b$label))
  pairs    <- combn(k, 2, simplify = FALSE)

  plots <- lapply(seq_along(pairs), function(pi) {
    p  <- pairs[[pi]]
    xi <- obj_names[p[1]]; yi <- obj_names[p[2]]
    xl <- obj_labels[p[1]]; yl <- obj_labels[p[2]]
    ggplot(df, aes(x = .data[[xi]], y = .data[[yi]], colour = run)) +
      geom_point(size = 1.5, alpha = 0.35) +
      scale_colour_manual(values = run_cols, name = "Run") +
      labs(x = xl, y = yl) +
      theme(legend.position = if (pi == 1) "top" else "none",
            axis.title = element_text(size = 9))
  })

  do.call(gridExtra::grid.arrange,
          c(plots, list(ncol = min(3L, length(plots)),
                        top  = textGrob(
                          sprintf("Pairwise Objective Scatter \u2014 %s", toupper(ECOSYSTEM)),
                          gp = gpar(fontsize = 13, fontface = "bold")))))
}

compare_pairwise_scatter(run_a, run_b, obj_names, obj_labels)
```

#### d) Spatial robustness: does seeding change which pixels are selected?

Pairwise Jaccard similarity of pixel selections across three groups: within run A's Pareto front, within run B's Pareto front, and cross-run (one solution from each front). If the cross-run distribution resembles within-run distributions, seeding does not substantially alter which pixels are chosen.

```{r}
#| label: compare-spatial
#| fig-height: 4

compute_cross_jaccard <- function(run_a, run_b) {
  if (is.null(run_a$df_psel) || is.null(run_b$df_psel)) {
    message("pixel_selection.csv not available for one or both runs.")
    return(NULL)
  }

  make_pixel_sets <- function(run) {
    psel   <- run$df_psel
    has_xy <- all(c("x", "y") %in% names(psel))
    psel   <- psel %>% mutate(
      pkey = if (has_xy) paste(round(x, 1), round(y, 1), sep = "_")
             else paste(pixel_row, pixel_col, sep = "_")
    )
    split(psel$pkey, psel$solution_id)
  }

  sets_a <- make_pixel_sets(run_a)
  sets_b <- make_pixel_sets(run_b)
  if (length(sets_a) == 0 || length(sets_b) == 0) return(NULL)

  rows <- lapply(names(sets_a), function(i)
    lapply(names(sets_b), function(j) {
      s1    <- sets_a[[i]]; s2 <- sets_b[[j]]
      inter <- length(intersect(s1, s2))
      uni   <- length(union(s1, s2))
      data.frame(jaccard = if (uni == 0) 0 else inter / uni,
                 type    = sprintf("Cross (%s \u00d7 %s)", run_a$label, run_b$label))
    })
  )
  bind_rows(unlist(rows, recursive = FALSE))
}

plot_jaccard_comparison <- function(run_a, run_b, obj_names) {
  jac_a <- compute_jaccard_pairs(run_a, obj_names)
  jac_b <- compute_jaccard_pairs(run_b, obj_names)
  jac_x <- compute_cross_jaccard(run_a, run_b)

  parts <- Filter(Negate(is.null), list(
    if (!is.null(jac_a) && nrow(jac_a) > 0)
      data.frame(jaccard = jac_a$jaccard_similarity,
                 type    = sprintf("Within %s", run_a$label)),
    if (!is.null(jac_b) && nrow(jac_b) > 0)
      data.frame(jaccard = jac_b$jaccard_similarity,
                 type    = sprintf("Within %s", run_b$label)),
    if (!is.null(jac_x) && nrow(jac_x) > 0) jac_x
  ))

  if (length(parts) == 0) { cat("Jaccard data not available.\n"); return(invisible(NULL)) }

  df_all <- bind_rows(parts) %>%
    mutate(type = factor(type, levels = unique(type)))

  ggplot(df_all, aes(x = type, y = jaccard, fill = type)) +
    geom_violin(trim = FALSE, alpha = 0.45, colour = NA) +
    geom_boxplot(width = 0.15, outlier.size = 0.8, fill = "white") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("#E05C2A", "steelblue", "grey50"), guide = "none") +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1),
                       limits = c(0, 1)) +
    labs(
      title    = sprintf("Spatial Similarity (Jaccard) \u2014 %s", toupper(ECOSYSTEM)),
      subtitle = "Pairwise Jaccard within each run's Pareto front and across runs",
      x = NULL, y = "Jaccard similarity"
    )
}

plot_jaccard_comparison(run_a, run_b, obj_names)
```
